discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single solid-state spins (nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond) and their use as quantum sensors
subfield: Quantum physics / solid-state spin qubits and quantum sensing
motivation: Wrachtrup and Jelezko first optically detected and coherently controlled individual electron and nuclear spins in a solid at room temperature, using the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond. They showed that a single atomic-scale defect can serve as a long-lived qubit that is read out with light. Lukin, with Wrachtrup and others, turned this into a new kind of measurement: nanoscale magnetometry with single spins. This made it possible to detect single electron and nuclear spins, map magnetic fields in condensed matter and image living cells. Together these advances made a fragile quantum property into a robust, engineerable platform. That platform started the field of solid-state quantum sensing, led to spin-photon entanglement and loophole-free Bell tests, and opened a worldwide search for new defect qubits in silicon carbide and other hosts. Today the platform is used in laboratories and emerging industry worldwide.
